chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Qattan narrated, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sukkari narrated, saying: Muhammad ibn Zakariya al-Jawhari al-Ghulabi al-Basri narrated, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ammara narrated, from his father, from Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, from Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) was asked: 'Where were you when Adam was in the Garden?' He said: 'I was in his backbone, and I was descended to the earth whilst in his backbone, and I rode the ship whilst in the backbone of Noah's father, and I was thrown into the fire whilst in the backbone of Abraham. Never did two parents of mine meet in fornication. Allah, Exalted and Glorious, did not cease moving me from the good backbones into the pure, purified wombs, a guided guide, until Allah took Prophethood as my oath, and Islam as my covenant, clarified everything of my characteristic, established my mentioning in the Tawrat and the Injeel, ascended me to His Heaven, and derived for me a name from His Names. My nation are the praisers, the One with the Throne is the Praised, and I am Muhammad.'
And this hadith has been narrated through many chains of transmission.
ai.seo_question: Where was Prophet Muhammad before Adam was created according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* articulates the Shia doctrine of the Prophet's pre-existence within the loins of the prophets, emphasizing his spiritual continuity from Adam to Muhammad. It highlights the concept of *Tahara* (purity) by noting that his parents never met in fornication, a key element in Shia genealogical theology, and asserts his prophetic identity was inscribed in previous scriptures. The narration underscores the divine selection process, linking his earthly mission directly to his eternal spiritual status.
